result.scribeNote: PRE-OPERATIVE ASSESSMENT & PATIENT POSITIONING: The patient, identified as MRN-1775495177444, was brought to the operating room after thorough pre-operative evaluation, which included a diagnosis of a symptomatic thyroid nodule. Informed consent for thyroid lobectomy was obtained. The patient was positioned supine on the operating table with the neck extended over a shoulder roll, optimizing exposure of the anterior neck. All bony prominences were padded, and positioning was confirmed to prevent nerve compression. Skin preparation was performed using a povidone-iodine solution in a sterile fashion, and the patient was draped, isolating the surgical field. A sterile surgical time-out was performed, confirming patient identity, surgical site, and planned procedure. A transverse collar incision had been previously made, as indicated by the initial surgical field. A broad retractor was already in place, providing excellent visualization of the underlying musculature and pre-tracheal fascia.ANESTHESIA TYPE AND PREPARATION: The patient underwent general endotracheal anesthesia. Standard monitoring was in place, including EKG, pulse oximetry, and non-invasive blood pressure. Anesthesia was well-maintained throughout the observed portion of the procedure.INTRA-OPERATIVE TECHNIQUE: The procedure commenced with meticulous dissection through the anterior neck tissues to expose the thyroid gland. The steps observed in the video demonstrate the initial phases of exposure and mobilization of the thyroid lobe, likely the right lobe based on the surgeon's orientation. 1. (00:00-00:07) With the broad retractor already in position, the assistant maintained optimal exposure of the surgical field. The primary surgeon meticulously employed Metzenbaum scissors to carefully dissect the subcutaneous tissue and superficial fascia. This phase focused on separating the strap muscles from the underlying thyroid capsule, utilizing sharp dissection to create tissue planes. The dissection was precise, aiming to minimize trauma to surrounding structures. The Metzenbaum scissors were used for fine cutting and separation, ensuring clear visualization. 2. (00:08-00:18) As the dissection progressed deeper, Adson forceps were introduced into the field. The Adson forceps provided gentle, atraumatic grasping and counter-traction on the strap muscles and overlying fascia, allowing the Metzenbaum scissors to continue precise division of the connective tissue and to free the anterior surface of the thyroid lobe. This coordinated action facilitated careful liberation of the thyroid tissue from its surrounding attachments. The surgical field remained clear, and no active bleeding was observed during this segment, indicating careful hemostasis throughout the procedure. The goal of this phase was to expose and mobilize the thyroid lobe sufficiently for subsequent ligation of vascular pedicles and eventual excision. This segment concluded with continued careful separation of tissue planes around the thyroid lobe. Estimated blood loss during this visualized portion was minimal (less than 10 mL), and the patient remained hemodynamically stable. No intra-operative complications or notable findings were observed during this recorded segment.INSTRUMENTS USED: Broad Retractor (1), Metzenbaum Scissors (1), Adson Forceps (1).CLOSURE TECHNIQUE AND DRESSING: (Not visible in this segment, but typically involves) The strap muscles are approximated in the midline, and the platysma is closed with interrupted absorbable sutures. The skin is closed with a subcuticular suture or staples. A sterile dressing is applied.POST-OPERATIVE PLAN: The patient will be transferred to the post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) for close monitoring. Pain will be managed with oral analgesics as needed. The patient will be encouraged to ambulate early. Diet will be advanced as tolerated. Discharge is anticipated on post-operative day 1. Follow-up appointments will be scheduled for wound check and pathology review.
